(Maybe I asked the wrong question... What if I tried
asking a different way?)

Was there a man here, deeply tanned and dressed kind of
flashy?

I'm really not supposed to blab about our customers, but you
don't look like the type who'll take no for an answer...
Yeah, he was here.
Really!?

Yup. But as you can see, he's not here anymore. He mentioned
that he still wanted a drink or two, so he could be hoisting
drinks elsewhere.
Thank you very much! Goodbye!
Hold it, little lady. We don't have any kid drinks here.

Welcome... Or not. You're an unfamiliar face. Sorry, but we
only cater to members.
This is the Nagasu branch of Kamiyama Works.
I, uh, don't have all that much merchandise, but I'm thinking I will gradually add more.
I specialize in weapons. I can do all sorts of things with weapons, as long as you pay.
I sell new weapons, and I can fix busted weapons, too.
Kamiyama's shop sells weapons and protective gear. Weapons can also be repaired if they have worn down through use.
I'm trying to go national, but I'm short on funds. I'm even having trouble sourcing materials for the main Kamurocho shop.
If you don't mind, could you donate materials you might not need?
If I get more funds, I can work on developing new weapons and gear.

You can invest in Kamiyama Works and raise its shop level by donating materials and cash. As the shop levels up, better weapons and gear will be added to the merchandise. Some items require specific materials to be donated.
While there are several Kamiyama Works shops, they all share the same shop level.
Got it. If I find something, I'll pass it on.
Thanks. If there's anything I can help with, don't hesitate to ask.
Welcome. We take pride in our amazing prizes here! We're practically breaking the bank to get these prizes to you. Want to hear about our fabulous prizes?

S Rank (1,500+ points)
Staminan XX
A Rank (1,300+ points)
Bronze Plate
B Rank (1,100+ points)
Toughness Z
C Rank (900+ points)
Iron Plate

S Rank (1,900+ points)
Tauriner Maximum
A Rank (1,700+ points)
Staminan XX
B Rank (1,500+ points)
Tauriner ++
C Rank (1,300+ points)
Tauriner +

Five Correct Answers
Special Pin-up Girl Photo (Collect all three!)
Staminan X (If all photos collected)

Three or More Correct Answers
Pin-up Girl Photo (Collect all three!)
Staminan X (If all photos collected)

All Panels Destroyed
One Pin-up Girl Photo (Collect all three!)
Staminan X (If all photos collected)
It's a lineup of prizes that could have me bleeding red ink by the bucket. But, don't worry about me⑬swing away, friend.
Not particularly.
Uh... Oh. Really? Well, take my word for it⑬we have great prizes up for grabs. Check us out.
(I only have what Christina said to go on. I guess I'll head to Shin-Osaka Station.)
Hi. Can you get me to Shin-Osaka Station?
Of course! Lots of people headed that way, huh?
Yeah, heh. I probably shouldn't be blabbing about this, but just between you and me, I gave a ride to a big pop idol a few minutes ago.
Do you know Haruka Sawamura? She's been on TV a lot lately, maybe you've seen her there.
Anyway, she was sitting right there not fifteen minutes ago! Boy, I knew she was cute from seeing her on TV, but I didn't realize she was that cute in person, too!
So she went to Shin-Osaka Station, too?
That's right. She was in a big rush. Work, I guess. Dangit, I should've gotten her autograph!
(Lucky he's the talkative type.)
Sorry, I forgot to pick something up from the store. I'll be back in a flash.
Yeah? You sure? If you hurry, you might still catch her at the station.
So if I hurry, I might catch her at the station? Step on it!
You got it! How can I let another Haruka fan down?
(Come to think of it, Noa Amon-san was waiting for me at Soten TV.)
(Hmm... Should I head over there now?)
(Okay, let's do this!)
(I can't afford the fare. Better scrounge up 640 yen...)
The base fare is 640 yen. Where are you headed?
Another city? Of course.
Hello, sir. You may purchase chips here.
Would you like to buy some chips?
Excellent. I'll get your chips ready.
Here are your 50 chips. Thank you.
Here are your 100 chips. Thank you.
Here are your 500 chips. Thank you.
Here are your 1,000 chips. Thank you.
Here are your 10,000 chips. Thank you.
I'm afraid you don't have enough money, sir.
Welcome to the blackjack table. You can play one game for as little as ten chips. Care to try your luck?
I've noticed that you play blackjack quite often. Would you be interested in playing the house, one-on-one?
All right, then. First, I'll need your 1,000 chips.
You paid 1,000 chips.
Thank you. Now, then, let's begin.
Very well. Let's continue with normal blackjack, then.
Excellent.
Would you like to see the rules?
I see. I hope you'll join us another time.
You seem to be short on chips. Please come back soon.
Tell me the rules.
This is a game between you and the house. Whoever gets three wins first wins the game.
Before the game begins, I'll need 1,000 chips for you to join. The payout differs depending on which deck is used.

Standard Deck: 2,000 chips
Without 2/3/4: 2,500 chips
Without 7/8/9: 2,000 chips
Without J/Q/K: 4,000 chips
If you win, you'll get the designated number of chips.
Welcome to the baccarat table. You can play one game for 1,000 chips. Would you like to play?
How would you like to play?
Would you like to go over the rules for Super 6?
Welcome. Would you care to join us for a round of poker?
An excellent choice. What stakes would you like to play for?
I'll go with the low stakes.
With low stakes, bets are made in five-chip increments in the first two rounds, and in ten-chip increments in the last two rounds.
Please take a seat.
You'll need a minimum of 100 chips to play low-stakes poker, sir.
I'll go with the high stakes.
With high stakes, bets are made in 50-chip increments in the first two rounds, and in 100-chip increments in the last two rounds.
You'll need a minimum of 1,000 chips to play high-stakes poker, sir.
Would you like to go over the rules for Pineapple Hold 'em?
Would you like to go over the rules for Omaha Hold 'em?
I see. We look forward to having you join us.
Thank you for always playing roulette with us. Recently, we added a new game mode called Survival mode. Would you care to give it a try?
This is a one-on-one match against the dealer. Both players have seven chips, called markers, that are placed on the table. The object of the game is to eliminate the opponent's markers.

Stop the ball on the opponent's number on the roulette wheel to remove its marker. Each player gets three tries, alternating back and forth. If you win, you earn a payout based on how many markers you have left.
Thank you for always playing roulette with us. Recently, we added a new game mode where you can play as the dealer. Would you like to give it a try?

In this mode, you play as the dealer. Drop the ball on the wheel depending on where the guests place their bets. Guests will bet more if they win. Try letting them win low bets to encourage higher betting, then make them lose big.
Hello. Would you care to join us for some roulette?
Would you like to play me one-on-one? It's a best-of-five match. While no outside bets can be made, the odds are doubled over the duration.
Very good, sir. Please take your seat.
It looks like you don't have enough chips to play roulette, sir.
I'm sorry. You need at least 10,000 chips to play Survival Roulette.
How about playing the house, one-on-one sir? You won't able to place outside bets, but you get five spins with double the odds.
I'm sorry, sir, but you need 1,000 chips to play as the dealer.
Would you like to go over the rules for roulette?
Hello. You can trade in your chips for prizes here.
Thank you. Please do come again.
Uncle Kaz! See if you can <Color:8>win 1,000 chips or more at roulette<Color:Default>. Beat the odds!
(Haruka wants me to <Color:8>win 1,000 chips or more at roulette<Color:Default>.)
Aww, okay. Well, I don't blame you.
Certainly. What would you like to do?
Certainly. Please be seated.
Sorry. I'm afraid you don't have enough chips to play roulette.
Would you like to go over roulette's rules?
I see. We look forward to having you join us. Please come again.
Thank you for always playing roulette with us. We just added the Survival Rules, which is a new game mode. Would you like try it?
This is a one-on-one match against the dealer. Both players have seven chips, called markers, that are placed on the table. The object is to eliminate the opponent's markers.

Stop the ball on the opponent's number on the roulette wheel to remove its marker. Both sides have three alternating throws each. If you win, you earn a payout based on how many markers you have left.
Thank you for always playing roulette with us. We've just added the Dealer Mode. Would you like to try it?
I'm sorry. You need at least 10,000 chips to play Survival Rules.
I'm sorry. To play the Dealer Mode, you must have at least 1,000 chips.
Hello. Would you care to join us for some poker?
Uncle Kaz! I bet you can <Color:8>win 2,000 chips or more at poker<Color:Default>. Your poker face is amazing!

Certainly. What would you like to play?
I'll go with low stakes.
With low stakes, bets are made in five chip increments in the first two rounds and in ten chip increments in the last two rounds.
I'm sorry. You need at least 100 chips to play low stakes poker.
I'll go with high stakes.
With high stakes, bets are made in 50 chip increments in the first two rounds and in 100 chip increments in the last two rounds.
I'm sorry, but you need at least 1,000 chips to play high stakes poker.

I'm sorry, but you need at least one hundred chips to play low stakes poker.
With high stakes, bets are made in 50 chip increments in the first two rounds, and in 100 chip increments in the last two rounds.
Very well. It costs 1,000 chips to join.
This table is for low stakes blackjack. You can play for as little as ten chips a hand. Would you like to play?
Uncle Kaz! See if you can <Color:8>win 1,000 chips or more at blackjack<Color:Default>. Hope you know when to stay!

You seem to be familiar with blackjack. Would you like to play me one-on-one?
Thank you. Let's begin our one-on-one game.
Would you like to go over the blackjack rules?
I'm sorry, but you don't have enough chips. Perhaps another time.
It's a one-on-one game between you and me. The first to get three wins is the victor.
You need to put up 1,000 chips in advance to play. The payout depends on the type of deck used.

- Normal deck -> pays 2,000 chips.
- No 2/3/4 cards -> pays 2,500 chips.
- No 7/8/9 cards -> pays 2,000 chips.
- No J/Q/K cards -> pays 4,000 chips.
If you defeat me in the one-on-one game with three wins, you get the indicated number of chips.

Congratulations! You managed to knock down the red pin!
You got a <Color:8>Low-resilience Jacket<Color:Default>.
Here's your prize. Please do come again.
Welcome. Is it just the two of you today?
It'll be 1,000 yen for two players.
Okay, got it.
(What should I do?)
You won't beat me, Uncle Kaz!
Give it your best shot, Uncle Kaz!
Have fun!
Sorry, not today.
Come on, let's bowl!
(Hinata wants to bowl with me.)
Good luck beating me!
How many frames will you play?
Three frames, please.
Ten frames, please.
Aww, guess it's a draw. But I'll beat ya next time!
That was wicked fun! I'm headin' back to Hakata now! <Color:255,200,200,255>⑮<Color:Default>
That was wicked fun! Call me again, okay? <Color:255,200,200,255>⑮<Color:Default>
You're real good, Akiyama-san! I'm kinda surprised!
Yeah, I win! Gotta try a little harder than that, Akiyama-san!
Wow, I can't believe it's a draw! Next time I'm definitely gonna win!
That was super fun! Now I gotta get back to Osaka. <Color:255,200,200,255>⑮<Color:Default>
That was a lotta fun! Gimme a call again, okay? <Color:255,200,200,255>⑮<Color:Default>
I win! Better luck next time, Saejima-san!
